canonicalInteraction.description: After content selection and optional source-rectangle editing, Add commits to the displayed track/time. A source file creates a full-duration unnamed occurrence; a named clip copies its full content definition into a fresh video-owned occurrence while retaining an origin association only for explicit library update. It has no live dependency on the library; later library changes leave it unchanged. A composed clip is copied as one grouped object and operations act on that group as a whole until Ungroup. New occurrences begin at 100% volume and unmuted. Inserting at a target edge shifts colliding later occurrences forward on that track; other tracks are unchanged. A saved video expands its complete description to fresh occurrences and preserves its relative timing, rectangles and audio; expansion is available only where the destination can preserve those settings. Conflicting track settings cause an atomic no-insertion result with the conflicting tracks identified. No nesting or live video reference is invented. During commit use video-saving; restore staged choices on failure.

name: Add
outcome: The complete addition succeeds atomically, or the unchanged draft and staged choices remain for correction.

patternBasis.rationale: Reviewable track-targeted insertion adapts established insert behavior; source cropping requires a staged selection before Add.

purpose: Commit the reviewed content, destination and source rectangle as one draft addition.

conditions: The Add dialog is open. Add is enabled only after content is selected and the reviewed destination, source rectangle and applicable compatibility checks are valid.

canonicalInteraction.description: Drag the selected occurrence's Start or End, or use the equivalent focused boundary command. End extension moves each later overlapping clip to the first frame after its predecessor, continuing only while a collision remains; intervening gaps absorb extension. End shortening leaves a gap and does not pull later clips backward. Start changes its source boundary and timeline start together, keeping its timeline end fixed; restoration stops at source bounds, time zero or the previous clip's end. Minimum duration is one frame. Preview the changed boundaries, pushed clips and resulting duration before completion. Invalid input or Escape leaves the original draft and selection. Source media and named definitions remain unchanged. For a grouped clip, the same Start/End edit acts on the whole group. Inward trim keeps hidden parts in the copied definition. Outward trim restores them and may include available source-file content at the corresponding edge, within the same source and timeline bounds; it never time-stretches playback. This is not a change to the saved library clip.

Change only that saved definition, for future additions; retain the selected occurrence and all other copies unchanged. Do not publish crop, audio or track settings. There is no downstream propagation or collision validation. During the actual commit preserve draft and selection and apply the existing commit freeze. Success identifies the updated clip and returns to the captured editor context. Failure changes nothing and retains the dialog, target and proposed values for retry or Cancel.

name: Update Named Clip
outcome: The library clip retains its identity with the reviewed Start and End; existing video copies, including the selected occurrence and its local trim, stay unchanged.

patternBasis.rationale: A familiar explicit update confirmation compares current and proposed values and identifies the one saved item changed; independent copies remove cross-instance propagation.

purpose: Update only the named library clip's reviewed temporal boundaries.

conditions: The update dialog is open with a valid target.

cancellation.description: Immediate local action, or native chooser/gesture cancellation as described in its outcome.

canonicalInteraction.description: Choose an empty-lane time, a target clip edge, or Append on the active track. Inside a clip, resolve to its nearest edge and show Before or After. With no explicit point, append after the active track's last clip, or time zero on an empty track. Keyboard time/edge selection is equivalent. Scrubbing and selection do not silently replace this insertion choice.

name: Insertion point
outcome: The target track and explicit time, Before/After target, or Append are shown without changing content.

patternBasis.rationale: Familiar desktop control and owner-defined behavior; specialized timeline manipulation is separately researched.

purpose: Choose the active track and composed-time destination for the next addition.

conditions: An active video exists; an empty timeline shows Append.

alternateInputs.description: Focus and activate a named track header.

cancellation.description: Selection is immediate and does not mutate composition content.

canonicalInteraction.description: Select one of four track headers. Track 1 is initially active. Show its output rectangle, volume and mute state. Changing tracks clears a whole-object selection on another track but preserves a composition-wide range. Show the new insertion track explicitly; do not reuse an insertion point belonging to another track.

name: Track
outcome: The active track and its properties are apparent.

patternBasis.rationale: An explicit active track makes destination and property scope apparent.

purpose: Identify the track receiving additions and track-level adjustments.

cancellation.description: Cancel closes Add without changing the original draft.

canonicalInteraction.description: Choose a project video file, named clip or saved video. Retain the displayed insertion destination. Files and named clips initially use their full source frame and permit Source rectangle editing. A saved video preserves its complete existing description; show compatibility with destination track settings. Changing the content resets staged crop values to that content's defaults. Only Add inserts content.

name: Content
outcome: The Add dialog identifies the chosen content and its applicable options without inserting it.

patternBasis.rationale: A familiar staged selection precedes an explicit Add command.

purpose: Stage content before reviewing its destination and source rectangle.

conditions: The Add to Timeline dialog is open and no commit is active.

cancellation.description: Cancel discards the staged rectangle and restores the captured stopped editor.

canonicalInteraction.description: From active-track properties, stop preview at the resolved frame and open the track's output rectangle. Capture its current values and return context. Identify that the change affects every occurrence on this track. The default is the complete output frame.

name: Output rectangle
outcome: A rectangle editor identifies the track and previews a staged output rectangle.

patternBasis.rationale: A clearly scoped property editor separates saved output framing from inspection.

purpose: Change the saved output area used by one track.

conditions: An active video and track exist and no commit or other modal decision is active.

cancellation.description: Cancel restores the captured occurrence editor or staged Add dialog without applying this crop.

canonicalInteraction.description: Open for exactly one selected occurrence, or for a staged file/named clip in Add. Stop preview and identify the content and source coordinate space. Start from the current occurrence crop, or the full frame for a new addition. A composed named clip uses its complete composed frame as this source. Editing a saved video's expansion preserves its existing occurrence crops; crop individual occurrences after expansion. Capture whether Apply should update the active draft or return to staged Add.

name: Source rectangle
outcome: A source-frame preview exposes the occurrence's staged crop without changing its underlying media.

patternBasis.rationale: The source crop has its own subject and coordinate space.

purpose: Choose the source area used by one occurrence.

conditions: Exactly one editable occurrence is selected, or a file/named clip is staged in Add.
No commit or competing modal decision is active.

alternateInputs.description: Enter the same rectangle using keyboard-operable percentage fields.
alternateInputs.input: Left, Top, Width and Height fields

cancellation.description: Cancel abandons the entire staged rectangle edit.

canonicalInteraction.description: Move or resize the rectangle in the identified full source/output frame. Keep the rectangle inside that frame and its width and height positive. Show Left, Top, Width and Height as percentages of that frame. Numeric entry is equivalent and validates complete bounds rather than silently distorting or clamping entered values. Preview the candidate without changing the saved draft. The selected source rectangle always fits proportionally within the output rectangle.

name: Rectangle
outcome: A valid candidate rectangle and its visual result are previewed; invalid inputs remain unapplied.

patternBasis.rationale: Direct adjustment and numeric properties are equivalent inputs to one rectangle operation.

purpose: Precisely adjust the staged source or output rectangle.

conditions: A source or output rectangle editor is open.

cancellation.description: Cancel restores the values captured on dialog entry.

canonicalInteraction.description: Set staged Left and Top to zero and Width and Height to 100%. This resets only the rectangle named by the dialog. It does not reset player inspection or another track/occurrence.

name: Full frame
outcome: The candidate rectangle covers the full source or output frame; Apply is still required.

patternBasis.rationale: A scoped reset restores an identified default before explicit application.

purpose: Restore the staged rectangle to its complete coordinate frame.

conditions: A source or output rectangle editor is open.

cancellation.description: Apply completes the local operation; completed draft changes use Undo.

canonicalInteraction.description: Require valid bounds and the captured target. For an existing track or occurrence, apply one undoable draft operation and refresh composed preview. For a source rectangle opened from Add, update only the staged addition and return to Add; the original draft remains unchanged until Add succeeds. Do not alter source files, temporal trim, named definitions or inspection zoom. If application fails, retain the rectangle inputs and original target values for correction or cancellation.

name: Apply
outcome: The valid rectangle updates one draft target or the pending Add choice.

patternBasis.rationale: An explicit application boundary preserves the distinction between preview, staged addition and draft mutation.

purpose: Apply the reviewed rectangle to its captured target.

conditions: The rectangle editor is open; Apply is enabled only for valid bounds and a valid target.

alternateInputs.description: Adjust the same percentage with pointer or keyboard.

cancellation.description: Invalid entry preserves the previous value; completed adjustments use Undo.

canonicalInteraction.description: In active-track properties, enter a value from 0% to 100%, initially 100%. A keyboard-operable slider may provide equivalent input. Apply to every occurrence on that track. The effective contribution is occurrence volume multiplied by track volume, unless either is muted. Keep mute independent; zero volume does not toggle mute. Preview valid changes during playback; a completed adjustment is one Undo operation.

name: Track volume
outcome: The track volume changes while occurrence volumes and mute choices remain independent.

patternBasis.rationale: Track-bound controls communicate that the adjustment affects multiple occurrences.

purpose: Adjust all audio contributions on the identified track.

conditions: An active track exists and no commit or modal decision is active.

cancellation.description: Toggle again or use Undo to restore the prior state.

canonicalInteraction.description: Toggle mute in the identified track header. Initially off. Show its current state and track identity. Muting affects audio only, preserves track and occurrence volume values, and is one undoable draft operation. A selected occurrence on this track identifies track mute as a reason it is silent.

name: Mute track
outcome: The identified track's audio is muted or restored without changing its picture or stored volumes.

patternBasis.rationale: Each repeated mute control has a distinct named track owner.

purpose: Silence one track without losing its volume setting.

alternateInputs.description: Adjust the same occurrence percentage with pointer or keyboard.

cancellation.description: Invalid entry preserves the previous value; completed adjustments use Undo.

canonicalInteraction.description: For exactly one selected occurrence, enter 0% to 100%, initially 100%. A keyboard-operable slider is equivalent. Keep its track volume and both mute settings unchanged. Show when track mute prevents an audible result. Preview valid changes during playback; one completed adjustment is one Undo operation. Ordinary audio edits never update the named clip definition.

name: Clip volume
outcome: Only the selected occurrence's volume changes.

patternBasis.rationale: Occurrence-bound controls remain distinct from their containing track.

purpose: Adjust audio for one occurrence.

conditions: Exactly one occurrence is selected and no commit or modal decision is active.

cancellation.description: Toggle again or use Undo to restore the prior state.

canonicalInteraction.description: Toggle mute for exactly one selected occurrence. Initially off. Preserve clip and track volume values, track mute and all picture content. Unmuting the occurrence does not unmute its track. Treat the toggle as one undoable draft operation.

name: Mute clip
outcome: Only the selected occurrence's audio mute state changes.

patternBasis.rationale: An explicit occurrence mute preserves independent track control.

purpose: Silence one occurrence without losing its volume.

conditions: Exactly one occurrence is selected and no commit or modal decision is active.

cancellation.description: Dismiss Selection actions before invocation without changing the draft. A completed Ungroup participates in draft Undo/Redo.

canonicalInteraction.description: With exactly one grouped occurrence selected, open Selection actions. Enable Ungroup only when the group source rectangle is full frame, group volume is 100%, and group mute is off, and its included parts can be represented on the destination track without overlap or changing the current picture and sound, including embedded composition framing, stacking and audio. On activation, replace the group with each part's portion intersecting the inclusive trimmed extent. Retain each part's own source rectangle, volume and mute, included source interval, relative timing and gaps; omit wholly excluded parts. The neutral group properties require no transfer, and part settings are not reset or discarded. Existing destination-track framing and audio continue to apply. Keep the resulting parts selected and the affected time visible; commit one undoable draft operation. If the group has a non-full-frame source rectangle, volume other than 100%, or mute on, show Ungroup as unavailable with the specific adjustment reason because its transfer policy is not defined, even when the parts do not overlap. Also keep Ungroup unavailable for overlapping/multitrack placement or other composition settings that cannot be preserved on the destination track without an undesigned mapping. Preserve the complete copied group, hidden parts, all settings, draft and selection in every unavailable or failed case. Never automatically reset properties to enable the command, bake adjustments, flatten, shift or remap tracks.

name: Ungroup
outcome: For an eligible group with full-frame source rectangle, 100% group volume and group mute off, replace it with the included portions of its parts on the same track. Retain each part's own source rectangle, volume and mute, its included source interval, relative timing and gaps. Omit wholly excluded parts. Keep the current picture and sound over the group's used extent, with the existing destination-track framing and audio still applied; do not reset or lose part settings. Keep the library clip unchanged and the resulting parts selected.

patternBasis.rationale: An explicit contextual break-apart command exposes constituent clips without adding a new workspace or content type. Trim filtering and copied ownership come from product authority.

purpose: Expose the included parts of one grouped clip for independent timeline editing.

conditions: Exactly one grouped occurrence is selected and Selection actions is open. Enable only when the group source rectangle is full frame, group volume is 100%, group mute is off, and included parts fit the destination track without overlap while retaining their own source rectangle, volume, mute and the current composition picture and sound.

Keep Ungroup visible but unavailable for nondefault group source rectangle, volume or mute, explaining each applicable adjustment whose transfer is undefined. Also explain nonrepresentable timing, placement or composition settings without selecting a mapping. No settings or draft content change.
Ungroup is unavailable while any draft or project commit is active.
